stories.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
stories.reason: Real, confirmed, high-detail supply-chain compromise: attackers pivoted from a leaked Fireworks AI key through Cursor's systems to ship a trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension for ~11 hours. Concrete scope numbers, part of the broader 'Black October' AI-platform breach wave.
key_facts: Attackers used a leaked Fireworks AI access key to read a Cursor-Fireworks data-sharing bucket of historical coding-agent traces (unredacted creds in some)
Malicious Claude Code extension versions 2.1.312/2.1.313 live ~11 hours, tried to install persistent SSH backdoors (buggy, often failed)
<0.05% of users had traces exposed, <0.01% had API creds compromised, up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious build
Part of a wider 'Black October' wave of breaches across AI dev platforms (Fireworks, Railway, Notion)

stories.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
stories.reason: FBI flash alert on Artex, an open-source LLM-driven pentest framework abused for state-speed intrusions (targeting->privileged access in <3hrs in some cases), 1,600+ exposed public instances found, DeepSeek Flash models dominating usage for lack of guardrails. This is the AI-driven-attack-automation story the taste profile is built around.
key_facts: Artex: open-source AI pentesting platform, turns any LLM into an autonomous intrusion agent; released by 'Autumn-27' in August, later abused and taken down but persists via forks/commercial version
FBI: some intrusions went from initial targeting to privileged access in under 3 hours
Censys found 1,600+ publicly exposed Artex console instances (actual deployments likely higher)
FBI says DeepSeek Flash models dominate usage for capability, low cost, and lack of guardrails when framed as pentesting
Targets: financial services, government, defense, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, telecom, legal

stories.title: Weight Space Misfolding
stories.reason: Genuine new AI x cyber research: a threat model and taxonomy for one model maliciously editing another's weights post-deployment (factual substitution, capability denial, selective omission), with controlled probes and real numbers showing current edits aren't cleanly localized, plus a proposed inspection framework. Directly adjacent to, but distinct from, the Lazarus neuron-backdoor story already covered.
key_facts: Defines 'weight-space misfolding': unauthorized weight edits by another model that violate the target's legitimate deployment constraints
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct probes via IWIBench editor: factual substitution succeeded 100/100 but broke an unrelated capability (couldn't say 'Sydney' anymore)
Legal-refusal edit worked on only 5/22 held-out prompts and broke an unrelated refusal; supplier-omission edit worked 1/22
IWIBench mean editing-skill reward rose 0.2148 -> 0.4250 in under 5 months; no demonstrated self-propagation or air-gap crossing
Proposes Deep Patch Inspection and Broad Weight Inspection as partial defenses, neither a general guarantee

stories.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
stories.reason: llama.cpp/ggml hit v1.0.0 after ~3.5 years — first real API/ABI stability guarantee for the backbone of the local-AI ecosystem (150+ architectures, used by countless downstream apps). A genuine infra milestone, not a feature drop.
key_facts: llama.cpp and ggml both reach v1.0.0; semantic versioning now signals API/ABI breaks to downstream devs
Project is ~3.5 years old; supports 150+ model architectures and mainstream speculative decoding
ggml backends can now be compiled as dynamic libs loaded at runtime
CI scaled via HF Buckets/Jobs with hardware-partner runners (NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, Intel)

stories.title: Serving GLM-5.3 at 607.8 tok/s across two Nvidia DGX stations with vLLM
stories.reason: Concrete serving benchmark on real hardware: 753B MoE (40B active) split across two DGX GB300s over 400Gb RDMA, hits 607.8 tok/s at concurrency 16 using TP=2, speculative decoding, FP8 KV cache. Exactly the inference-infra substance this feed is tuned for.
key_facts: GLM-5.3 NVFP4, 753B total/40B active params, ~464GB checkpoint
Two DGX GB300 (252GB HBM3e each) linked via ConnectX-8 RDMA at 400Gb/s, TP=2
607.8 tok/s aggregate at concurrency 16 (peak); 107.4 tok/s at concurrency 1
Per-user throughput falls from 115.3 tok/s (c=1) to 13.0 tok/s (c=32)
Uses 4-token speculative decoding, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching, FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE backend

stories.title: Lovable apps expose passport details and more than 200K private messages
stories.reason: Not fetched, but title and scale (599 pts, passport details + 200K private messages) match the exact pattern of the already-covered 'Grok apps leak passwords/hospital data' story — AI app-builder (Lovable) shipping no-auth-by-default apps that leak sensitive data at scale. Strong fit for the AI x cyber line even unread.

stories.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
stories.reason: Deep, concrete personal research dive: 600 experiments isolating exactly where JEPA world-model planning fails (hierarchical subgoals, latent-memory graphs, pusher-aware scoring), with honest negative results and a harder benchmark the author built. Low-saturation, high-signal — the discovery tier's reason for existing.
key_facts: LeWM (JEPA world model) on Push-T: swapping in exact simulator physics barely changes long-horizon success (78% vs 77%) — the learned predictor isn't the bottleneck
Hierarchical planning (subgoal every 25 steps) raises 75-step success from 22% to 80%, beating exact-physics flat planning (42%)
Latent memory graph w/ jump cost reaches 85% success, matching expert-subgoal planner
Pusher-aware goal scoring doubles hardest-test success from 11% to 23%
Author's new harder benchmark (250 episodes, cross-demo start/goal) caps best planner at 56% success

stories.title: Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity by funding AI startups to buy its GPUs
stories.reason: Extremely high-engagement (1025 pts) story directly about AI-compute economics — Nvidia allegedly funding AI startups specifically to buy its own GPUs, engineering scarcity. Already-seen territory at this point level, but headline score isn't penalized for saturation per Mine.
